detail.longDescription: I'm running into an issue with hosting some code on an AWS Lambda. I'm trying to run a project on a Lambda with the following file structure: my_layer.zip/ └── python/ # This folder name is mandatory └── my_package/ # Actual package folder ├── __init__.py # Required so Python treats it as a package └── other_subdirectories ├── __init__.py └── file_I_wanna_use.py I then want to call functions in file_I_wanna_use.py from the lambda, but I am running into error module my_layer.file_I_wanna_use has no attribute class_I_wanna_use I believe this is because the structure of the code in the layer shown above is incorrect in some way, but can't figure out why exactly. Edit: Here's the lambda file that I'm trying to call a function on the layer with: import Layer import json def lambda_handler(event, context): result = Layer.agents.agent_liflow01.WorkflowHelperLI.chat() return { 'statusCode': 200, 'body': json.dumps({'message': result}) } And I'm getting this as the error message, where agent_liflow01 is a file that has the class I want to access: { "errorMessage": "module 'Layer.agents' has no attribute 'agent_liflow01'", "errorType": "AttributeError", "requestId": "fbf7fc3a-e907-4629-90c0-094cdd470b4b", "stackTrace": [ " File \"/var/task/lambda_handler.py\", line 5, in lambda_handler\n result = Layer.agents.agent_liflow01.WorkflowHelperLI.chat()\n" ] } The error message is almost identical if I don't include the .agent_liflow01 portion.
